title: This episode cost $102,725 and took 45 days to make.
html:
1/12

This episode cost $102,725 and took 45 days to make.

...but I think we've finally solved AI Filmmaking.

We made MAJOR breakthroughs in audio + cinematography.

And Part II (next week) is even more insane.

Steal our brand-new process and Dreamina prompts below👇🏼🧵 https://t.co/39T7urOiuZ

2/12

Story:
This episode is an homage to my favorite movie of all time, Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind.

For 20 years, I've wanted to create something like this, and AI finally makes that dream possible. https://t.co/Ml9FafdBul

3/12

This is the first time we're bringing together episodes from separate Nexus episodes.

Up on until this point, the previous 7 episodes have been R&D on us seeing what characters and plots resonated most with the audience.

This will be the first time we're doing a linear story across multiple, connected episodes.

We're VERY excited to show you more of Anika (from Ep 1 - Wet Market) and Jace (from Ep 4 - Squid Hiest).

This is Part I of Episode 8, and we'll be doing a part II and III over the next two weeks as they figure out how to escape the ship and steal an invaluable resource from the empire.

We will then continue the linear episode progression until the end of January where we will finish in a BIG FINALE for Season 1 with all the characters in an epic showdown against the empire.

4/12

With this post for Part 1, i'm mostly going to focus on audio, but at a high level, here's an overview of the process:

Character Sheet / Ingredient Exploration:

Tell Claude to list all the characters/props/vehicles you'll need to create character sheets for.

Then choose your favorite Canvas tool to work with the agent and create dozens of variations for each element.

we like going "wide" with gpt 2.5 sunburst and then going "deep" (hi res) with our selects by redoing them with Seedream 5.5

5/12

Then do location plate shots exploration:

Next week i will give you the FULL GUIDE for this because it's actually really critical to our new "anamorphic emulation" look we acheived with this film.

In short, use Seedream 5.5, a 21:9 aspect ratio, and prompt with as many anamorphic descriptors as you can.

A huge part of the look from your footage is determined by your background plate.

6/12

Now that you have ingredients + location plates, you can have Claude split your script into scenes and then those scenes by 30 second sequences/prompts.

I'm going to include a few examples of prompts below and then include my Claude skill below.

We didn't do any 3D workflows for this film because it was wayyyyy to complicated and we had a large team so it was actually easier to just use the ingredients based approach.

This is where you have Seedance do a pass at each scenes from many angles, and then we take screenshots of our favorite angles and get closeup coverage the second time we animate a scene.

The first animation pass lets you lock where everyone is, and the second pass has the screenshots anchor those locations but you can get deeper/closer coverage of everyone in those exact locations.

this isn't always necessary, though, a lot of scenes we can cover in one pass.

We organize all our scenes in the canvas so we can work with multiple animators, who take point on different scenes and our director for this episode, Beau, can give direct feedback and orchestrate all our animators in real time.

7/12

Let's look at a favorite scene of our animators 😂

Anika and Jace changing out of their prison uniforms and into mechanics uniforms.

Here's the prompt:
[NEXUS - PRISON BREAK - P1 SC5S - INT. MECHANIC BAY - THE DISGUISE / "I HAVE A SHIP" - CAMERA A, ENGINE ROOM - 28s - 8 SHOTS, ENTIRE SCENE HANDHELD, OPENS ON ANIKA AT THE WALL MAP - v10]

@7e08dad0-b824-4e33-af04-720a3217e8fd - Mechanic bay, the AUTHORITATIVE location. Architecture, materials and lighting only, not the framing. Cathedral-scale boiler hall: pale blue-white riveted steel columns banded in brass, glowing furnace hatches, brass catwalks and lanterns, pipework, valves, deep navy shadows, steam.

@682a7dae-aa97-4901-bc2e-f79a9e233c98 - Imperial prison ship, the AUTHORITATIVE design for ONE MAP ONLY: the LARGE FRAMED MAP MOUNTED UPRIGHT ON THE BAY WALL, styled as in @Image6, is a drawing of this exact vessel in fine dark ink on worn cream paper, matching its silhouette. The real ship never appears. MAP FRAMING LOCK: the map is a set piece, never the subject: only ever at an angle and soft, never straight on, never an insert.

@706fbad2-5148-499a-8707-77efda253c4f - ANIKA, PRISON CLOTHES. Face, scars and costume authority. Pale skin, black hair loosely pinned up with loose strands, dark eyes, two long diagonal scars down her forehead and cheek. Weathered orange and black prisoner tunic, 381 on the back, studded leather belt, orange trousers, boots. Ignore the pale undershirt in the sheet: she wears NO undershirt.

@f6ea2995-d6a0-4786-9c66-a50b6b96873c- ANIKA, ENGINEER DISGUISE. Costume authority for the final shot. Dark navy-charcoal zip-front work jumpsuit with tan sleeve stripes and the pale spire-in-crescent emblem, riveted leather shoulder guards, leather gloves, a dark tool belt with an ornate buckle and pouches. Same face and scars as @Image3. Ignore the wrench.

@2d35de6e-6379-48e6-975c-29831f5a158e - JACE, NEW LOOK. Face and costume authority. Dark wavy black hair, grey-blue eyes, light stubble, age 27. A worn black one-piece work jumpsuit with a stand-up collar trimmed in brass piping and a front zipper, sleeves rolled, leather knee pads, tall brown leather boots. Ignore the sheet's goggles and blurred face.

@28b9ee06-ef39-40f6-bd44-7e0a6263a5be - STILL FRAME, REFERENCE ONLY, NEVER A SHOT: only for the WALL MAP and the look around it: the prison ship drawing in fine dark ink on aged cream paper in a heavy dark wooden frame on the wall, warm lamp light across it; Anika at the map in her orange 381 tunic; shirtless Jace soft behind her. Never its framing, never a first or last frame. Ignore all map lettering.

@c7db08b7-a317-4e01-8359-30c1d0efa07f - SECOND STILL FRAME, REFERENCE ONLY, NEVER A SHOT: ONLY for what is BEHIND THE MAP: a solid pale blue-white riveted steel wall. Never its framing, never a first or last frame, never Anika's pose or costume from it.

BRACELET LOCK: each wears ONE ornate black and gold bracelet with a dark gem: Anika on her LEFT wrist, Jace on his RIGHT. Gems dark, no chain.

ENVIRONMENT: the @Image1 mechanic bay, at the foot of the boiler hall. A freestanding waist-height schematics table with an open tool case and notepad; a few steps away a large map of the prison ship is mounted upright on a riveted wall panel between two columns. WALL LOCK: the map hangs flat on a SOLID pale blue-white riveted steel wall, visible at its edges, as in @Image7; no gap or void behind it, never floating or freestanding. BACK-TO-JACE LOCK: Anika stands right in front of the wall map, FACING THE WALL, her BACK to the room and to Jace. Jace is a few steps BEHIND her, by the schematics table. When he looks at her scars, he is looking at her back.

CAST LOCK, ABSOLUTE: ONLY TWO PEOPLE are in the bay for the whole scene: ANIKA and JACE. No one else anywhere, no figures on the catwalks or stairs. Anika stays at the wall map; only in Shot 6 does Jace walk a few steps along the table.

COSTUME LOCK: Jace starts with the black @Image5 jumpsuit on his legs, the top half hanging empty at his waist by its sleeves, SHIRTLESS above. He puts his arms into the sleeves and zips it up the front to the collar. Anika starts in her orange prison tunic and removes it; her hands stay free, she holds nothing.

GOGGLES LOCK, ABSOLUTE: in Shots 1 to 5 Jace's head is BARE, dark wavy hair uncovered, NO goggles on his head, forehead, neck or anywhere on him; the brass goggles lie on the schematics table and he first touches them in Shot 6.

FINAL LOOK LOCK: Anika's last frame MATCHES @Image4 EXACTLY: the jumpsuit already worn open down to mid-chest, a deep open V neckline with natural cleavage and the edge of the tan wrap bra in the V, the collar unfastened and spread flat, shoulder guards and straps on, tool belt at the waist. NO ZIPPING BY ANIKA, ABSOLUTE: she never touches her zipper; the neckline never changes. The only zipper that moves is Jace's, in Shot 6.

BRA LOCK, ABSOLUTE: under the orange tunic Anika wears ONLY a TAN WRAP BRA: plain worn tan linen strips wound snugly around her chest like a binding, knotted at the side, strapless, low enough to show natural cleavage. Never a sports bra, crop top, tank top or lace, no straps or cups. The same tan wrap in every shot; its edge shows in the V of her jumpsuit at the end.

SCARS LOCK: Anika's LOWER BACK shows exactly TWO DEEP OLD CUT SCARS: two long slashes across her lower back just above the belt, none on her stomach, long healed but deep, thick ridged tissue with sunken grooves, pale-to-pinkish, never more than two, never fresh or bleeding.

VOICES, text only, accents held in every line:

ANIKA: a clear GENERAL AMERICAN accent: low alto, dry, flat, practical; NOT British, NOT Estuary, NOT English-sounding in any way; never raises her voice.

JACE: light working-class British Estuary accent, southeast England, not Cockney, not posh, not American. Warm mid-range voice, a light rasp on emphasized words; sheepish when caught; when anxious his words speed up, never shouting.

MECHANIC BAY LIGHTING, DRAMATIC: low-key, high-contrast chiaroscuro. Deep navy-black shadows fill most of the frame. Hard warm orange furnace glow rakes in low from one side; cold blue light falls from high above through the steam, rim-lighting hair and shoulders. THE ENGINE ROOM IS ALIVE BEHIND THEM: thick steam billows and vents from pipes and valves in the background, catching the light in visible shafts between the columns; furnace fire flickers behind open hatches, huge pistons turn slowly in the haze. Never flat, never evenly lit.

BACKLIGHT FROM PRACTICALS: both are lightly backlit in every shot by a visible source behind them: a caged brass work lamp on a hook by the table and the furnace glow through the steam, a soft warm rim on hair, shoulders and face edges.

LANDING LOCK, ABSOLUTE: never open, settle or end on a frame like @Image6 or @Image7: never Anika in side profile at the map, never a frontal medium shot of her flat against it.

Tech spec: Photoreal live-action feature film, no CGI look. vintage 2x anamorphic, 2.39:1, native 21:9, organic 35mm grain. VERY SHALLOW DEPTH OF FIELD in every shot, focus on faces, eyes and hands; furnace fire, lit steam and lanterns become large vertical OVAL BOKEH in amber and pale blue. No crushed blacks.

CAMERA, ENTIRE SCENE HANDHELD: every shot is a physically operated handheld camera with breathing, subtle sway and late corrections, moving only when a character motivates it. No tripod, dolly, gimbal, crane or digital zoom. Natural blinking and breathing, precise lip sync. No cloning.

SHOT 1 (0-4s) - ANIKA, REMOVING THE ORANGE / JACE'S EYES WANDER - handheld medium close-up, three-quarter angle from beside the wall map: @Image3 ANIKA facing the map, her back to the room, studying its routes; without looking away she opens the front of her orange tunic, pulls one arm free, then the other, and the top drops to hang from her belt, revealing the tan linen wrap bra and her bare back. Behind her, soft but readable, JACE by the schematics table, shirtless, bare head, NO goggles, the upper half of the black jumpsuit in his hands: he notices her changing, his attention drifts to her and HIS EYES WANDER over her figure, subtly checking her out, a flirtatious curiosity, lingering a little longer than they should. NO smile, no smirk, no eyebrow play: it is all in his eyes.

SHOT 2 (4-6s) - JACE, ATTRACTION TO REALIZATION - 85mm intimate handheld close-up on Jace by the schematics table, one arm partly in the jumpsuit sleeve, eyes on Anika. START: face relaxed, mouth neutral, a subtle appreciative interest in his eyes, his gaze wandering: he finds her attractive; his eyes do the flirting, no smile. Then HIS GAZE TRAVELS DOWN HER BACK to the two deep healed scars: the flirtation leaves his eyes, they STOP wandering and SETTLE ON THE SCARS; brows draw together slightly, eyes narrow a fraction, his face goes still: attraction turning to genuine curiosity, trying to understand what happened to her. No shock, no pity, no disgust, no dramatic concern. The change is entirely in his eyes; his mouth stays neutral throughout. He says nothing. CUT ON HIS EYELINE.

SHOT 3 (6-7.5s) - THE SCARS, JACE'S VIEW - intimate handheld close-up from behind her at Jace's angle on her LOWER BACK: the tan wrap band at the top of frame, the orange fabric and belt at the bottom; the two long, deep, fully healed scars, thick ridged tissue and sunken grooves, old, never fresh or bleeding; a subtle handheld push, very shallow focus on the scars, the wall map soft beyond her.

SHOT 4 (7.5-10s) - "EYES." - handheld close on Anika's face from beside the wall map, Jace soft behind her over her shoulder; she knows he is looking; she never turns, her back still to him; cool, dry, clipped, not angry - ANIKA: English: {Eyes.} - RACK FOCUS to Jace: his eyes snap away at once, head turning slightly, caught; a brief flicker of embarrassment; he plays it off: on "Sorry" a small self-conscious hesitation and a tiny dismissive hand gesture; "I was just looking at your..." a little more sincere, meaning the scars, then realizing it may make it more awkward, trailing off - JACE: English: {Sorry, I was just looking at your...} - warm, slightly sheepish; no second apology, no nervous laugh, no broad smile.

SHOT 5 (10-13s) - "WHAT? YOU WANT THE WHOLE STORY RIGHT NOW?" - 50mm handheld medium close-up as Anika turns from the map to Jace, the operator easing around with her. She looks straight at him: calm, mildly incredulous, eyes narrowing slightly, a small pointed look; dry, snarky, a little attitude; not serious, defensive or wounded. "What?" quick, a little sharp, a tiny lift of her eyebrows, reacting to his timing, not asking him to repeat; "You want the whole story" dry, sarcastic disbelief, head tilting slightly, eye contact held; "right now?" a little extra emphasis, a pointed, almost teasing challenge, not louder - ANIKA: English: {What? You want the whole story right now?} - mouth mostly neutral, eyebrows slightly up, mild exasperation; no eye roll, no smile. Not upset he saw the scars, only incredulous he wants an explanation mid-escape.

SHOT 6 (13-21s) - JACE, LAUGHING OFF THE IMPOSSIBLE - handheld close-up on Jace: he meets her eyes, glances down, no second apology, turns his back to her and keeps it turned; AT FIRST, soft in the bokeh behind him, Anika begins changing in her tan wrap bra, pulling the navy-charcoal jumpsuit up over her hips. He pushes his arms into the black jumpsuit sleeves and zips it to the collar, then walks four or five slow steps along the table, and the handheld TRACKS WITH HIM, leading him, so Anika slides out of the background and EXITS THE FRAME; on the walk he picks up the brass goggles and settles them on his forehead, where they stay. HE NEVER LOOKS BACK AT HER. He can't quite believe any of this and tries to laugh it off WITHOUT laughing. A little breathless, dryly disbelieving, subtle nervous humor: "Okay." a small exhale, organizing his thoughts, a faint disbelieving breath through his nose: right, so this is happening; "I don't know you." a light gesture back toward her without turning; "You don't know me." a gesture to himself, eyebrows lifting slightly, listing the absurd facts; "We're stuck to each other" a glance down at the bracelet on his RIGHT wrist, a small incredulous head shake, the faintest disbelieving half-smile, never a full smile; "and there are bugs eating people." a little quicker, more animated, repeating terrible news he hasn't accepted, a tiny breathy release through his nose, not a laugh, eyes widening slightly, brows up, mouth back to neutral - JACE: English: {Okay. I don't know you. You don't know me. We're stuck to each other and there are bugs eating people.} - shoulders lifting briefly, still walking: humor as a defense, processing bad news in real time; no laughter, no grin, no shouting.

SHOT 7 (21-24s) - "TELL ME YOU HAVE A PLAN." - he stops walking and only now turns back toward her for the first time since Shot 6; the attempt at humor fades; sincere, quiet anxious hope, a little vulnerable, almost pleading - JACE: English: {Tell me you have a plan.} - the operator follows his eyeline toward her.

SHOT 8 (24-28s) - "I HAVE A SHIP." - handheld push past Jace toward Anika at the wall map, now wearing the navy-charcoal engineer jumpsuit, the orange gone, already dressed exactly in the @Image4 FINAL LOOK, open V at the chest - rack focus: Jace falls soft into the bokeh as she comes sharp - she turns to him, one hand giving a small tug to her leather shoulder guard strap, her hands never at her chest or zipper, the deep V and spread collar unchanged, one eyebrow lifting slightly, confident, faintly amused, no smug grin - ANIKA: English: {I have a ship.} - the push lands on a TIGHT close-up of her face from a low three-quarter angle past Jace's soft shoulder, steam and furnace glow behind her, the map only a soft sliver at the frame edge, never the frontal medium shot of @Image7 or the profile of @Image6 - HOLD ONE FULL SECOND on her expression after the line: eyes on Jace, quiet confidence, no new words, only breathing and a blink - then HARD CUT.

DIALOGUE LOCK, ABSOLUTE: the six lines written in the shots, in that order, word for word, are the ONLY words spoken in the entire clip. No ad-libs, no extra or repeated lines, no names, no 'hey' or 'what', no muttering, whispering or mouthing, no voiceover. Between lines both stay silent.

Sound design: <deep engine vibration>, <heavy machinery and pistons>, <steam venting through pressure valves>, <furnace roar>, <tunic fastenings opening>, <fabric rustling>, <boots on metal>, <Jace's jumpsuit zipper pulled up once, in Shot 6 only>, <quiet breathing>. OFF-SCREEN BATTLE, VERY LOW, muffled through the hull: <distant shouting>, <aircraft engines>, <dull explosions>. No music, no subtitles, no on-screen text.

8/12

Here's all the ingredients that went into that prompt. https://t.co/QOhc3rgiJS

9/12

Here's a flying sequence prompt:

[NEXUS - WORLD NINE - EXT. FORGOTTEN FOREST / ANCIENT HIVE RUINS - DEEP TWILIGHT - BOMBING RUN - THE HIVE / SOMETHING BENEATH THE FOREST - CAMERA C, 100mm - 28s - 11 CUTS - REAL TIME 24 FPS, NO SLOW MOTION - NATIVE 21:9 - CODE 99 - v1]

@29b39349-5fd8-4e56-8b9a-1647198a3f73[CAPTAIN] - Look reference only, match the sheet exactly: older male Empire Navy pilot, swept-back greying hair, gold-rimmed goggles, silver-and-gold respirator, ivory and gold Imperial flight coat, white fur-trimmed collar, dark leather harness, gloves. Ignore the helmet he holds on the sheet. He is the CAPTAIN flying the LEAD Falcon fighter. His respirator stays on; his performance reads through the eyes, brow and small head turns. Voice: British, low, controlled, weathered, quietly authoritative. Voice only.

@b435f8f5-6965-4373-9bc5-0812a795b900 [PILOT] - Look reference only, match the sheet exactly: female Empire Navy pilot, dark hair in a long braid, brown eyes, gold-and-brass breathing mask exactly as the sheet, ivory flight suit with gold embroidery, brown leather cross-harness, gloves. Ignore the helmet she holds on the sheet. She flies a SEPARATE Falcon alongside the Captain. Voice: British, young, bright, playful, self-satisfied. Voice only.

@69f90c3f-7252-47ff-b1bc-e29983f84986 [HIVE TARGET] - References are inspiration only, do not recreate. NEVER use this image as a shot, a first frame or a last frame, and never match its composition, camera height or framing. It only shows WHAT the target is: the large ruined stone complex on the LEFT side of the canyon, inside the hand-drawn blue circle: enormous carved stone faces, ancient columns, collapsed temple walls, overgrown terraces and stairs, set deep in a misty forest canyon with dark conifers, cliffs and distant waterfalls. The blue circle is an annotation only: never render it. ONLY the circled complex is bombed; never the waterfalls, the river, the ruins on the right or a generic mound. Environment only.

@9e24a398-6f33-4e37-a190-90866dc03ad6 [BOMBER] - Exact design, never altered: the large white-and-gold Imperial flying-wing bomber, wide gothic wing, ivory riveted panels with gold filigree, glazed brass-ribbed nose, domed top turret, twin tail fins, rows of big brass propeller engines, a mechanical belly bomb bay. Far larger than the Falcons. Prop only.

@fca8d0ac-a975-46b4-943f-47bd4e1e75c7 [FALCON] - Exact design for EVERY escort fighter, never altered: twin ivory-and-gold booms joined by a tail spar, a centre pod with a bubble canopy, a pusher propeller, gold fleur-de-lis and eagle insignia, nose cannons. Aircraft never transform or swap designs. Prop only.

@9fa9d4f7-aae8-4ef2-82ea-4ddf4657f2ab [CREATURE] - Creature appearance only: thick overlapping brown armored scales, irregular weathered ridges, organic segmented plates, small fin-like structures. Its SCALES are the only detail ever seen. Never framed as head, eyes, mouth or full body in this scene.

@b5ffbb66-deb8-47d3-a27c-b2d459141d0a @1d33a97a-7e51-4ca2-99b5-12d6594a0a44 [BUGS] - Creature appearance only: Joe's established alien bug designs, every bug matches them. Medium-density scattered clusters and streams with large pockets of open sky; never a solid swarm.

REFERENCE LOCK: no image is a shot, a first frame or a last frame.

Scene context: the subject is the Empire, and the scene resolves on the Captain's realization. The creature is a FRAGMENT ONLY for the whole scene: a long winding ridge of earth travelling under the trees, trunks leaning in sequence, roots lifting, and ONE brief patch of armored scales breaking the soil. Never its head, eyes or full body. Geography never flips: the bomber and both Falcons stay in FAST, CONTINUOUS FORWARD FLIGHT, SCREEN LEFT TO RIGHT, high above the canyon, never hovering, stopping or reversing; the bug battle stays ACTIVE around them throughout, bugs moving independently at every depth; the bomber passes DIRECTLY over it; the bay opens on the belly; brass-studded, egg-shaped bombs drop in quick succession and fall VERTICALLY while the bomber keeps moving forward; the fireball rises ONLY from the circled complex; the aircraft are already flying away to the right when it erupts, the blast BEHIND them. Every aircraft is propeller-driven with visibly spinning propellers in every exterior cut; no jets, no afterburners, no jet exhaust. Separate cockpits; no radio, hands never leave the controls. The underground movement begins only AFTER the explosion and travels AWAY from the ruined complex into the adjacent forest in one continuous serpentine path with a clear leading point; it is not a shockwave. Real time throughout. Resolves on the ridge continuing into the dark valley.

DIALOGUE, ABSOLUTE: EXACTLY TWO LINES, in this order, lip-synced behind the masks where visible: @Image2 (cut 5): English: {That's what you get for messing with the empire.} @Image1 (cut 8): English: {What is that?} No other words, no radio chatter, no announcements, no cheering, no narration.

CAMERA C: Anamorphic 2.39:1, 21:9, photoreal ARRI Alexa register, subtle vintage 2x anamorphic character - EVERY cut on the SAME long 100mm lens, nothing wider - no lens flare - very shallow depth of field - dirty framing through propeller discs, wingtips, tail booms, canopy frames, bug wings and mist - no cloning - Hollywood acting - natural motion blur, organic grain. SHAKY HANDHELD throughout: exteriors feel shot handheld from a chase plane door and from the forest floor, the long lens compressing aircraft, bugs, canyon and blast into stacked layers, the operator fighting wind and vibration with constant small shake, sway, late reframes and quick corrections; cockpits are handheld inches from the pilots, the frame trembling with the airframe. Documentary-raw, Paul Greengrass handheld, never jittery to the point of blur. Motivated rack focus carries the story: eyes, canopy reflections, the forest below. Scale reads through compression and partial framing, not width. Oval bokeh, subtle lens breathing. No floating camera, no hovering camera, no zoom, no speed ramps, no slow motion.

LIGHT: HIGH CONTRAST deep twilight: cool blue-grey overcast sky, faint lavender cloud edges, dark desaturated forest greens, pale mist in the canyon. Dim overcast skylight is the key, thick canyon mist, deep readable shadows; the aircraft stay mostly in shadow with thin cool highlights along their metal edges. Small warm instrument lights on the pilots. The explosion throws a brief strong orange reflection into both cockpits; as the Captain notices the movement, that warm light fades off his face and he returns to cool ambient light. No sunrise, no peach horizon, no visible sun, no teal push, no electric blue, no bloom.

CONTINUITY LOCK: same Captain from Pilot 27 and same female pilot from Pilot 23, in separate Falcons; the bomber keeps its exact design; fast forward flight and spinning propellers in every exterior cut; the bug battle never stops; bay doors open while the bomber is moving; the bombs fall under gravity; cut 3 descends WITH the bombs, the ruins starting FAR below and growing; cut 3 cuts straight to the blast; the blast is at the circled complex only; the aircraft are already flying away with it behind them; she celebrates first, he notices second; his satisfaction turns slowly to confusion and concern; no radio; ONE continuous serpentine body underground; one brief surfacing of scales; no full creature reveal.

CUT 1 (0 to 2.5s) - 100mm shaky handheld from a chase position, tight and compressed on the @Image4 bomber racing past, a slice of its massive wing and spinning propellers filling the foreground, the operator swinging to keep it - the bomber and @Image5 Falcons race SCREEN LEFT TO RIGHT in escort formation through an ACTIVE bug battle, @Image7 @Image8 bugs crossing close to camera, behind the fighters and around the ruins; FAR below in the canyon the circled complex, carved faces and columns, passes directly beneath the bomber -

CUT 2 (2.5 to 5s) - 100mm shaky handheld from below, tight on the bomber's belly racing overhead, the frame shuddering as the operator tracks it - the belly bay doors swing open on rivets and hinges, the brass-studded egg-shaped bombs disengage and drop in QUICK SUCCESSION while the bomber keeps racing forward overhead, bugs still streaking through the airspace -

CUT 3 (5 to 7.5s) - FALLING WITH THE BOMBS: 100mm shaky handheld dropping ALONGSIDE the payload, tight on the bombs, wind buffeting the frame, never a distant side angle - the bombs fill the foreground and midground, accelerating under gravity; above, the bomber recedes out of frame still flying forward; FAR BELOW, deep in the canyon, the circled complex starts SMALL, showing the huge vertical distance, then grows rapidly as mist rushes past and bugs cross at different depths; strong parallax, real-time 24fps, never slowed or suspended in mid-air - CUT DIRECTLY TO THE EXPLOSION as they reach the target -

CUT 4 (7.5 to 10.5s) - 100mm shaky handheld trailing the aircraft, the long lens stacking the fighters, bugs and the blast into one compressed frame, the operator rocking with turbulence - the bomber and Falcons already racing away to the right in the foreground, propellers spinning at speed, small banks as they clear the target; BEHIND them the circled left-side complex erupts, a huge orange fireball over the stone structures, smoke, dust and debris rising through the canyon, the shockwave rolling across the treetops, the blast receding as they gain distance; the bug battle stays active, nearby bugs scattering from the blast, some whipping past close to camera as fast silhouettes -

CUT 5 (10.5 to 14s) - tight close-up on @Image2 in her Falcon cockpit, still flying fast, 100mm, handheld trembling with the airframe vibration - gloved hands on the controls; the orange glow of the distant blast reflects across her face and her gold-and-brass mask through the canopy; baseline, she glances back toward the fading fireball; recognition, it worked; her eyes narrow with proud amusement; the corners of her eyes crease as a confident smile forms under the mask; she almost enjoys it a little too much - playfully proud, easy and self-satisfied, never angry, never shouted, a spontaneous moment of personality: English: {That's what you get for messing with the empire.} -

CUT 6 (14 to 17s) - intimate close-up on @Image1 in the lead Falcon cockpit, 100mm, handheld shaking with the engine - gloved hands steady on the controls; a soft orange reflection from the blast fading across his goggles; baseline, quiet satisfaction, a faint smile in his eyes; then something outside catches his attention; his gaze shifts down toward the forest; he turns his head slightly to the side of the canopy and leans just enough to see without leaving his flying position; the smile begins to leave his eyes; he squints; his brows draw together - confusion replaces satisfaction -

CUT 7 (17 to 19s) - his POV looking down through the canopy frame, 100mm, handheld juddering with the aircraft, the forest compressed into dense layers - at first only dark conifers across the misty valley, the ruins smoking far behind; then a long stretch of forest moves IN SEQUENCE: one group of trees leans, another shudders farther ahead, a winding ridge of earth travelling between them along a serpentine path as the aircraft flies over it; not a shockwave from the blast; something moving on its own beneath the trees; the frame follows it briefly -

CUT 8 (19 to 21s) - extreme close-up on @Image1's eyes, 100mm, handheld shake settling to a tense near-still - the warm reflection gone, cool light on his face; his satisfaction has vanished; his eyes widen just slightly as they track the movement; genuine uncertainty, concern growing, a thread of fear; he speaks naturally inside the cockpit, no radio handset, no microphone, hands never leaving the controls, eyes fixed below - quiet, involuntary, controlled but unsettled, never shouted: English: {What is that?} -
